title: GitHub Commit Weekly Commit Window Trend
dataSources: GitHub repositories (`github:repo`), commits (`github:commit`), issues (`github:issue`), and releases (`github:release`).
app: GitHub repository metadata, commit activity feeds, issue trackers, and release publish logs forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=github:commit commit_minutes=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(commit_minutes) as avg_duration, max(commit_minutes) as worst_duration by _time
| sort _time
description: Trends the average and worst commit window for GitHub commit events each week.
value: Weekly timing trends show whether a process is becoming slower, more erratic, or healthier over time.
implementation: Capture commit_minutes on each event and review weekly averages plus worst cases during your personal ops review.
visualization: Line chart of weekly average commit window with markers for the worst week.
grandmaExplanation: It records whether GitHub commit tasks are taking longer than they used to and where the slow weeks were.
